verification_note: Each value was read twice from its PDF by two independent automated readers on 2026-10-09. The reads agreed on 272 of the 279 rows transcribed (all 279 rows here, including 17 estragole and methyl eugenol rows and 1 methyl N-methylanthranilate row). The 7 disagreements were settled from the PDF's own text lines, where each row reads '<value> <substance CAS> <NCS name>' (checked against Palmarosa oil, 82.4 % geraniol): 5 kept the first read, and Styrax extract (0.1) and Styrax oil, Honduras (0.05) took the second for benzaldehyde. No value has been checked by a person against the printed page. Correct a value by editing its row; every row carries its source PDF.
source: IFRA Standards, Amendment 49 (2020), Annex I 'Contributions from other sources' tables, as copied by PerfumersWorld; one PDF per restricted substance (source_url on every row). Each value is the highest concentration of that substance reported in that natural.
scope: Only the 20 restricted substances with a Category 4 limit in ifra_cat4_51.json, and only rows for naturals Kenny owns and their close variants. Safrole (IFRA_STD_179) has no per-natural table, only its 0.01 % notebox total, so the safrole in nutmeg is not counted. Annexes of other restricted substances were not read.
stock_rule: A stock maps to the NCS rows that are that natural, not its part or species variants. Where the species, part or extraction is uncertain, every candidate is listed and the highest value per substance is used. Rows that print one substance under several CAS numbers (cedrene) also take the highest value, never the sum.

Labdanum Resinoid.note: No resinoid row; species, part or extraction uncertain: the highest value across these candidates is used (solvent extracts; the distilled oil row is excluded).

Magnolia EO.note: Kenny identifies the stock as Michelia alba; its extraction is not recorded. Michelia alba extract is the only Michelia alba row, so it is used as the only candidate.

Red Mandarin EO.note: Red mandarin oil is a mandarin oil (Citrus reticulata). The mandarin oil row (methyl N-methylanthranilate) and the tangerine oil rows (same species) are both candidates; the highest value per substance is used. The terpeneless mandarin row is a concentrated fraction and is not used.

Sandalwood EO.note: Species not stated; species, part or extraction uncertain: the highest value across these candidates is used.

Vietnamese Benzoin Tincture.note: Siam benzoin is Styrax tonkinensis from Vietnam and Laos; the tincture is read at the extract value.

Benzoin Resinoid.note: Siam or Sumatra not stated; species, part or extraction uncertain: the highest value across these candidates is used.

Orange Peel EO.note: Species not recorded: sweet (Citrus sinensis) or bitter (Citrus aurantium) orange peel oil; both are candidates. Annex I lists no bitter orange peel oil row for the substances read, so the sweet orange peel oil row is the highest value. The IFRA table applies the stricter bitter orange direct limit (IFRA_STD_088).

Peru Balsam Resinoid.note: Annex row is the oil; the resinoid may differ.

Turkish Storax Tincture.note: Turkish storax (Liquidambar orientalis) is not named; species, part or extraction uncertain: the highest value across these candidates is used. Honduras styrax is another species and is not used.

Grapefruit FCF Oil Sicilian.note: No furocoumarin-free grapefruit row; the grapefruit oil row is used.

Pine EO.note: Species not stated; the dwarf pine needle oil row is the only pine row.

Anise EO.note: Stock is Chinese anise: anise seed (Pimpinella anisum) or star anise (Illicium verum) is not recorded; species, part or extraction uncertain: the highest value across these candidates is used.

Elemi EO.note: Canarium luzonicum essential oil: the oil row, not the gum or resinoid rows.

Aurantiol.basis: Aurantiol is the Schiff base of hydroxycitronellal (C10H20O2, 172.27 g/mol) and methyl anthranilate (C8H9NO2, 151.16 g/mol) with loss of water (18.02 g/mol): 305.41 g/mol. 172.27 / 305.41 = 56.4 % of its mass is hydroxycitronellal, counted toward the hydroxycitronellal Category 4 total. The methyl anthranilate share has no IFRA standard of its own.
Aurantiol.source: stoichiometric calculation. IFRA_STD_043 (Amendment 51, read 2026-10-09) sets Category 4 at 2.1 % and does not mention Schiff bases, so counting this share is a conservative project choice, not an IFRA instruction.
